transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. I came in because... well, I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. It's just this constant feeling that I'm a bad employee and a bad homeowner, and that honestly, I just deserve to lose everything I've worked for.
Have you been feeling depressed most days?

Yeah, pretty much. When I really look back at it... the low mood and just losing interest in everything, it's been there for almost the entire time since this all started. I mean, there have been a few brief periods where I felt like I could function a little better, but mostly... yeah, it's just been a constant thing.
Has this low mood been present continuously for at least two years?
Yeah, it has. The depression and... well, just the loss of interest in things, it's been with me for about two years and one month now.
Before this current two-year stretch, had you ever gone through another period of depression that lasted at least two weeks?

No, not that I can remember. Before this started a couple of years ago... I mean, I had bad days, sure, but nothing that lasted for two weeks straight or felt like this. I was doing pretty okay before all of this hit.
During the past two years, was there ever a stretch of two months or longer when the depression lifted completely?

No, definitely not two months. Um... like I said earlier, there were maybe a few brief periods where I felt a little lighter or functioned a bit better, but it never completely went away for that long. It's been pretty much there the whole time.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different parts of your life?

Not really, no. I mean... I have normal stress, but I wouldn't say I worry excessively about a bunch of different things. It's more just the... the feeling down and the lack of energy that takes over, rather than feeling anxious or worried all the time.
During these past two years, was there ever a time when you felt completely free of depression for at least two months?
Um, I think you might have just asked me that one... but no. Like I said a minute ago, I've never had a two-month break from it. It hasn't ever fully gone away for that long.
During this two-year period, was there ever a time when your depression became clearly worse than usual for at least two weeks?

Um, I'm not really sure if it was exactly two weeks, but... yeah, there are definitely times when it gets a lot heavier. Like, the baseline is always kind of low, but sometimes it just dips even further and everything feels a lot harder to do. I don't know if I ever tracked exactly how long those worse periods lasted, though.
During one of those times when your depression got worse, was there ever a stretch of at least two weeks when you had five or more depression symptoms most of the day nearly every day?

I'm honestly not sure. I mean, I know it gets worse sometimes, but I haven't really sat down and counted up the symptoms or tracked if it was exactly five of them for two weeks straight. It's just... it just feels heavier, you know? But I can't really give you a specific number of symptoms like that.
During the times when your depression feels worse, do you have trouble sleeping?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um, most nights I just lie awake for hours, listening to the house settle. And then, even if I do fall asleep, I usually wake up around three or four in the morning. After that, I just can't get back to sleep before I have to get up for work.
During those times when your depression gets worse, do you notice a clear drop in your appetite?

Yeah, my appetite gets pretty messed up. Um, it's all over the place, really. Mostly, I just end up skipping actual meals during the day. I'll just sort of live on coffee and toast, or whatever is easiest to grab. I don't always notice it right away, but then I'll realize my clothes are fitting a lot looser than they used to.
During those times when your depression gets worse, do you have trouble concentrating?

I haven't really noticed that, no. I mean, work can be stressful and sometimes I'm just tired from not sleeping, but I wouldn't say I have a hard time focusing on things or getting my work done. It's more just the physical tiredness than my brain not working right.
During the times when your depression gets worse, do you feel unusually tired or low on energy?

No, not really. I mean, I'm tired because I'm not sleeping well, like I said, but it's not like I can't get out of bed or do my job. I still have enough energy to get through the day and do what I need to do. It's just normal tiredness from being awake half the night, not some deep exhaustion.
During those times when your depression gets worse, do you move or speak noticeably more slowly than usual?

Yeah, actually, I do. I know I just said I have the energy to get my job done, but physically... I definitely move a lot slower. Um, especially some mornings at work. It's like just opening my spreadsheets or typing out responses takes forever. Even walking to a meeting, it literally feels like I'm pushing through wet cement. I still do what I need to do, but everything is just sort of in slow motion.
During the times when your depression gets worse, do you have thoughts that you’d be better off dead or of hurting yourself?

No, I don't have thoughts like that. I mean, I feel down and frustrated, especially with the sleep stuff and moving so slowly, but I've never wanted to hurt myself or thought about dying. That's not something I deal with.
During one of those worse periods, did you feel worthless nearly every day?

Yeah, I do. Actually, that's a big part of why I decided to come in. I just can't stop feeling like everything that goes wrong is my fault. Um, I feel like a terrible employee, like I'm failing at my job, and even at home... I just feel like a bad homeowner. It gets to the point where I genuinely feel like I deserve to lose everything I've worked so hard for. It's just this constant feeling of being completely worthless.
During those times when your depression gets worse, do you feel hopeless?

No, I wouldn't say I feel hopeless. I mean, I feel really bad about myself and my abilities, like I said, but I don't feel like things are never going to get better or that there's no point in trying. I still try to push through it all, hoping it'll eventually pass.
During one of those worse periods, did you lose interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy nearly every day?

Yeah, I definitely do. Um, I used to be pretty active with things outside of work. I'd plan brunches, paint in the spare room, go hiking... I even used to sign up for networking events. But when things get worse, all of that just stops being fun. It’s like... they just feel like tasks I’m pretending to care about, rather than things I actually want to do.
